title: arXiv AI papers — Friday, 13 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from visible independent coverage, conference signals, cross-list breadth, and released artifacts. The selected papers are very recent, so citation evidence is limited and does not establish readership or popularity.

sections.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
sections.abstract: The paper formalizes one-sided verifiability, where a verifier can reliably reject failures but cannot certify positives, and proposes NOPO, which learns by suppressing trusted negatives; reported experiments improve pass@k across code, logic, and math tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose reference-relative negative suppression plus a group-level update adapter, and report better pass@k under unit-test, constraint-check, and LLM self-verifiers when oracle rewards are unavailable (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the paper's reported code, logic, and math benchmarks and its one-sided-verifier setup; the abstract does not establish results in broader deployed settings.
sections.ranking_evidence: Accepted as a NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight; cross-listed in two core AI categories; independent paper write-ups/listings include OpenTrain and AI Safety Hot. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations when checked; this is an early total, not a period gain.

sections.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
sections.abstract: AgentSSL treats semi-supervised learning as agentic program search and reports that agent-generated pipelines beat human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings, while program selection can erase gains and is tested with a 16,977-program benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors frame semi-supervised learning as program search, introduce ProgramSelectBench, and report gains over human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 controlled settings (arXiv abstract and paper text).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that AgentSL matches AgentSSL on both ecology tasks and say the search is biased toward SSL; selecting programs without reliable labels remains unresolved (paper discussion).
sections.ranking_evidence: NeurIPS 2026 paper and conference poster; cross-listed in two core categories; independent analyses include BedrockNews and EigenRadar. Those write-ups converge on the program-selection bottleneck, rather than providing a popularity metric.

sections.title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
sections.abstract: The authors inject objective errors into real papers to measure reviewer detection and false positives, and introduce Skepthical, a tool-using multi-agent reviewer; across 30 papers and 357 injected errors, model choice and task-specific tools materially affect detection.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide an error-injection evaluation pipeline and Skepthical, which combines citation retrieval, computer algebra, and executed code for checking specific claims (arXiv abstract and paper text).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly say the benchmark measures localized objective defects, not holistic review quality; each field corpus contains only 15 papers, and the human adjudication check is limited (paper limitations).
sections.ranking_evidence: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026; spans three core AI categories plus digital libraries; independently summarized by Bharat Hunt, Foorilla, and arXiv.deeppaper. Citation momentum is not established for this very recent paper.

sections.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
sections.abstract: Metal Sandbox provides isolated native macOS execution and command scheduling across Macs for GPU coding agents; experiments on four Mac mini M4 nodes report higher command throughput under concentrated demand and lower waiting in fixed-trace scheduling replays.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine per-instance file restrictions, native command execution, and cross-Mac scheduling, reporting 1.68×–2.05× throughput in concentrated-demand tests and an 18.8% mean-wait reduction in fixed-trace replay (arXiv abstract and paper text).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the system is not hostile multi-tenant containment and does not guarantee GPU exclusivity; the scheduling replay holds agent behavior and phase durations fixed (paper discussion and limitations).
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in three core AI categories and distributed computing; code and Harbor integration are public; independent technical listings include arXivLens and Papers.cool. These are breadth and availability signals, not measured readership; citation evidence is sparse.

sections.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
sections.abstract: PixVid fine-tunes a pretrained latent video diffusion model to generate frames directly in pixel space, and the authors report higher-resolution output at the same per-frame token count, improved fast-motion control alignment, and frame-level response to actions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors replace the VAE output path with a framewise pixel-space design and report competitive VBench quality after fine-tuning from Wan2.1-14B (arXiv abstract and paper text).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report 3.9× as many tokens per second of video as Wan2.1 at 480×832, making short low-resolution clips more expensive (paper conclusion).
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper has a project page, independent technical summaries including AGI Hunt and Paperium, and a public author announcement. It is a useful signal from the vision category, but has no core-category cross-list or citation momentum confirmed in this snapshot.
